description: Cordelia's five attempts to convince Elijah to abandon his mission. Each escalates in emotional investment, tracking her transformation from self-interest to genuine care.

attempts.cordelia: You know they will execute me. Why waste your time escorting a corpse?
attempts.elijah: You will receive a trial. That is more than most of your kind offer their victims.
attempts.subtext: She is testing him, seeing if he wants her dead.

attempts.cordelia: You have seen how they frame the innocent. You have seen how little truth matters to power. And you still believe a trial will be just?
attempts.elijah: I believe it must be attempted.
attempts.subtext: She is genuinely confused by his faith in a system that failed him.

attempts.cordelia: Come with me. Not forever, just away. You could do more good in a year of hunting than a lifetime of serving those men.
attempts.subtext: She is starting to care about his fate, not just her own.

attempts.cordelia: You are a good man, Elijah. Perhaps the only one I have met. And they will destroy you for it, just as they will destroy me. We could live. We could matter.
attempts.elijah: I matter now. This matters. What we are doing, the children safe, the truth carried forward, it matters.
attempts.subtext: She is offering him everything she wishes someone had offered her when she left vampire society.
She stops asking. He notices. She has accepted something: her fate, his choice, or both.

thematicFunction: The five attempts track Cordelia's transformation from detached self-interest to genuine love for another person's wellbeing. Each attempt reveals more about her emotional state than about her argument.
